config.hypothesis: LoRA on permissively licensed, human-annotated finance data (news and tweet classification and entity extraction from Sujet-Finance, plus FinQA and TAT-QA questions with their calculations) improves exact-answer finance reasoning of the 4B base, measured on the held-out FinQA and TAT-QA test sets (FinQA in the gold-facts setting: the supporting facts are given, so it is not comparable with retriever-based leaderboards) and MMLU-Pro business and economics, without degrading general knowledge.

mmlu-pro.provenance: 12k 10-option questions in 14 categories; used per category for domain and regression evals.

finqa-test.provenance: FinQA test split, 1,147 questions, gold-facts setting (see finqa-train). Scored against the program's result (0.5 % tolerance; a percentage may be written as such) or the annotated answer; yes/no questions by yes/no. The dev split is not registered.

tatqa-test.provenance: TAT-QA test split with gold answers (tatqa_dataset_test_gold.json), 277 documents, 1,663 questions. Numbers are scored with a 0.5 % tolerance ignoring scale words, % and $; spans by normalized exact match; multi-span as an unordered set. The dev split is not registered.

sujet-finance.provenance: Subset of an aggregation of 18 public finance datasets, chosen by the `dataset` column after a license audit. Kept: the four classification and entity-extraction sources above (no QA), uploader-claimed MIT or odc-by; the news and tweet text in them is third-party. Excluded: gbharti/finance-alpaca (text-davinci-003 and GPT-3.5 outputs, CC BY-NC), dylanalloy/ehc-contrived-financial (OpenAI davinci-turbo outputs), amphora/lmsys-finance (GPT-4 and Claude outputs), financial_phrasebank and its copies AdaptLLM/finance-tasks_FPB, KennNguyenDev/FiQA_Financial_Phrasebank_Combined, AdiOO7/llama-2-finance (CC BY-NC-SA 3.0), AdaptLLM/finance-tasks_FiQA_SA (FiQA, non-commercial), AdaptLLM/finance-tasks_Headline and _ConvFinQA (no license; ConvFinQA overlaps FinQA), ceadar-ie/FinTalk-19k (answer provenance unverified), nickmuchi/financial-classification, lighthouzai/finqabench and adityamavle/FinRiskAnalysis (unknown provenance or LLM-generated).

finqa-train.provenance: FinQA (Chen et al., EMNLP 2021): questions over S&P 500 earnings reports written by financial experts, with the supporting facts and the calculation program annotated. 6,251 questions. GOLD-FACTS setting: the prompt gives the annotated supporting facts (`gold_inds`) and no retrieval is involved, so scores are not comparable with retriever-based FinQA leaderboards. The training target is the annotated program rendered as lines such as "5829 - 5735 = 94", then "Answer: <annotated answer>". Rows whose annotated step results contradict their own arguments (385 of 6,251, e.g. "2.5 / 1.6 = 0.9" or a lost minus sign) are dropped, so the model is not taught wrong arithmetic; the test split is not filtered.

tatqa-train.provenance: TAT-QA (Zhu et al., ACL 2021): questions over tables plus text from financial reports, annotated by finance experts. 2,201 documents, 13,215 questions (span, multi-span, count, arithmetic). The repository LICENSE is MIT; the Hugging Face card says CC BY 4.0, both permissive. The training target is the annotated derivation (when there is one) and "Answer: <answer> <scale>".

oasst2.provenance: Human-written conversations collected by OpenAssistant (2023); only reviewed, non-deleted, non-synthetic messages are used.
